title: Omiš with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Costs & Verdict
metaDescription: Planning Omiš, Croatia with a dog in 2027: dog beach, old town and restaurant rules, ferries, accommodation fees, summer heat, vets and EU pet passport.
content:
## Is Omiš dog-friendly?

Omiš works well for dog owners who plan around heat and leash rules. It is a small town of about 15,000 people where the Cetina river meets the sea, and everything is compact. Dogs are tolerated in the old town and on many restaurant terraces. Official dog beaches are few, which is typical for the whole of Dalmatia. Croatia has very few officially marked dog beaches, but almost every destination has spots where a dog can swim.

## Dog beaches in Omiš (plaža za pse)

### Almissa campsite dog beach
The best-documented dog area is a section of beach at the east end of the Camp Almissa beach (formerly Camp Galeb), at the entrance to Omiš on the road from Split. The beach is sandy with shallow water, which suits small dogs and puppies. Dogs should be on a leash outside the designated section.

### Brzet beach
Brzet is also widely listed as a pet-allowed beach in Dalmatia lists. It lies between Nemira and Omiš, has pebbles, and is surrounded by pine trees, so there is natural shade. A bar, café and restaurant are close by, and the beach has a public shower and toilet. The designation has been attached to different beaches over the years, so check for a sign on arrival or ask the tourist office on Trg kneza Miroslava.

### Other beaches
Outside the marked areas, the rule is simple: dogs are not welcome on the busy town beaches in season. This includes Velika plaža (Punta), the sandy beach at the Cetina mouth, with its beach bars, sunbeds and watersports. Many municipalities in Croatia restrict dogs on organised beaches in summer. In practice, quiet pebble coves and out-of-season walks along the shore are usually fine. Look for signs showing a crossed-out dog before you settle in.

## Dogs in the old town, restaurants and cafés

The old town is a set of narrow stone lanes under the Mirabella and Starigrad fortresses. It is flat enough for easy walks, and dogs on a leash are accepted. Stone paving gets very hot at midday in July and August. Test it with your hand, and walk before 9:00 or after 19:00.

Restaurants and cafés decide for themselves. Terraces generally accept leashed dogs. Indoor dining rooms often do not, because Croatian hygiene rules limit animals where food is prepared and served. Ask before sitting down, and carry a water bowl.

The marketing for the Fortica hike and the zipline makes Omiš look like a great outdoor base for dogs, but it is not. The Fortica trail is exposed, rocky and shade-free, and a dog should not do it between June and September.

## National parks, nature parks and the Cetina

Omiš has no national park inside the town. The nearest large protected area is Biokovo Nature Park, to the south-east above Makarska. Krka and Plitvice national parks are the well-known ones within a day trip or a longer drive. Both generally require dogs on a leash. Swimming areas, boats and some trails have restrictions, so check the park's current rules before buying tickets.

The Cetina canyon is the highlight for a dog and owner on foot. Riverside paths and the road to Zakučac are walkable, but rafting and canyoning tours do not take dogs.

## Ferries and catamarans

Omiš has no regular island ferry. Most visitors go to Brač, Hvar or Šolta from Split, about 26 km away, or from Makarska to Sumartin on Brač.

- Jadrolinija local ferry lines carry dogs free of charge. Dogs must wear a muzzle and be on a leash. Officially, they stay on deck.
- Rules on fast catamarans are stricter and vary by operator. Some accept only dogs in a carrier. Confirm with the operator before booking, because the captain can order a dog off the vessel if it causes complaints.
- Large dogs on some routes may need a deck pet box, which is booked in advance and costs extra.

## What accommodation charges for a dog

Pet fees in the Omiš area are usually €5–15 per night. Some apartment owners charge a flat cleaning fee of €20–50 instead. Hotels often limit dogs to certain rooms and may apply a cap on size. Campsites commonly charge a daily dog rate that falls in the same range. Many private apartments accept dogs, and filtering by "pets allowed" before booking saves wasted messages. Ground-floor units with a small terrace or garden are the most practical choice. Always confirm the fee and any breed or weight limit in writing.

## Summer heat and best months

July and August regularly reach 32–36 °C in Dalmatia, and sea water is warm, so there is little relief in the water. Hot asphalt and stone can burn paws. Never leave a dog in a parked car.

The best months are May, June and late September to October. Air temperatures are 20–28 °C, beaches are quieter and restrictions on dogs are looser. Winter is mild and also fine for walks, but many restaurants close.

## Vet basics

Omiš has a small number of veterinary services, and Split (about 26 km) and Makarska (about 35 km) have larger clinics. Emergency out-of-hours care is concentrated in Split. Save the contact details of a clinic before travelling.

- Ticks are common in the hills and along the Cetina. Check your dog after every walk.
- Sandflies in the Mediterranean can carry leishmaniasis. A repellent collar or spot-on product is worth discussing with your vet before travel.
- Fresh water is scarce on trails. Carry at least 1 litre per dog for half-day walks.
- A microchip is mandatory for every dog in Croatia.

## EU pet passport rules for driving in

From 22 April 2026 a new EU regulation (2026/131) replaced Regulation 576/2013. Traveller rules are almost unchanged and existing passports remain valid. A dog entering Croatia from another EU country needs:

1. An ISO microchip, implanted before the rabies vaccination.
2. A rabies vaccination, given at least 21 days before travel to a dog aged at least 12 weeks.
3. An EU pet passport issued by an authorised vet, or an animal health certificate if arriving from outside the EU.

In Croatia a passport costs about €10 plus VAT. Border checks are rare inside the Schengen area, but carry the documents. Drivers from the UK need an animal health certificate for each trip. Coming from Bosnia and Herzegovina or Montenegro, a dog must have the passport and enter through designated crossings.

## Verdict: how dog-friendly is Omiš?

Omiš rates about 3.5 out of 5. The dog-friendly points are a designated beach area, leashed walks in the old town and on terraces, free dog travel on Jadrolinija ferries, and many apartments that accept pets. The weak points are the limited number of official dog beaches, the heat in summer and the lack of shade on hikes. It is a good choice for a spring or autumn trip with a leashed, heat-tolerant dog and a ground-floor apartment. It is a poor choice for July and August with a short-nosed or senior dog.

faq.question: Is there a dog beach in Omiš?
faq.answer: Yes. A dedicated dog section sits at the east end of the Camp Almissa (ex-Galeb) beach, at the western entrance to Omiš. Brzet beach, with pine shade, is also widely listed as pet-allowed. Look for on-site signs, because designations have changed over the years.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on Omiš town beaches?
faq.answer: Not on the busy organised beaches such as Velika plaža (Punta) in summer. Quiet pebble coves and out-of-season beaches are usually fine with a leashed dog. Always check for signs showing a crossed-out dog.

faq.question: How much do hotels and apartments charge for a dog in Omiš?
faq.answer: Expect about €5–15 per night, or a one-off cleaning fee of roughly €20–50. Hotels may restrict dog size or limit pets to certain rooms. Confirm the fee in writing before booking.

faq.question: Can dogs go on ferries and catamarans from Split?
faq.answer: Dogs travel free on Jadrolinija local ferry lines, with a muzzle and leash, and officially on deck. Fast catamaran rules vary by operator, and some require a carrier. Check with the operator before booking.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia by car?
faq.answer: A microchip, a rabies vaccination at least 21 days old and an EU pet passport. Travellers from outside the EU, such as the UK, need an animal health certificate. Carry the documents even though border checks inside the EU are rare.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Omiš with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June and late September to October. Temperatures are 20–28 °C and beaches are quieter. July and August often exceed 32 °C, which is hard on dogs.

quickAnswer: Omiš is moderately dog-friendly. It has a designated dog beach area (at the Almissa campsite, with Brzet also listed), leashed dogs are fine in the old town and on most terraces, and accommodation usually charges €5–15 per night. Visit in May, June or late September. A microchip, rabies vaccination and EU pet passport are required.
